key_insight: The paper introduces a learned iterative NMPC solver that exploits temporal decomposition so the network size no longer grows with the prediction horizon, while preserving the same training objective and iteration update.
engineering_relevance: This makes real-time nonlinear MPC more scalable for large, fast systems by reducing online solve time without sacrificing constraint handling in closed loop.
method: Learns primal-dual updates toward KKT satisfaction via self-supervised training, avoiding precomputed optimal solutions.
Replaces a monolithic dense architecture with a temporally decomposed solver whose parameter count is independent of the horizon.
Uses closed-loop resampling to better match the training distribution to deployment conditions.
evidence_signal: On an economic NMPC CSTR cascade benchmark, the method scaled to larger problems than monolithic LISCO, achieved median speedups of up to 4× over IPOPT, and showed comparable closed-loop performance with no observed constraint violations.
watch_item: The approach is benchmarked on a specific NMPC setting, so performance and robustness may depend on problem structure and the quality of closed-loop resampling.
paper_title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
